The metaphors deepen the story’s emotional meaning: “capability being the only currency I knew how to spend in her presence” reveals Paul’s difficulty expressing love except through practical help. His mother’s observation that a house without something ripening is “just a waiting room” connects gardening with vitality and resistance to aging. The King Farouk and George Washington Carver allusions also enrich the family’s distinctive, gently humorous voices.
